title: Guscomquorom
summary: A Babylon neck name interpreted as a crossing place, linking Great East Neck with trail or wading-place memory toward Santapaug.
address_label: General Great East Neck area, West Babylon, NY
introduction_content: Guscomquorom is Tooker's placename for Great East Neck in Babylon. Earlier in the book he lists Caus Cung Quaram as a cross-reference to this fuller entry. Quoriac, also written Quoriack, is treated as an abbreviated related form in a Babylon meadow record.
history_content: A 1688 will by Jonas Wood mentions meadow either at Quoriack or at Tantamuntatauket; that dated reference is listed in the timeline.
translation_content:
Recorded forms include Guscomquorom, Guscomqiwrom, guscomquaram, Cans Cung Quaram, Caus Cung Quaram, and Caus-kum-cru-a-ran. The name is interpreted as a crossing place, possibly because an Indian trail crossed the neck or because there was a wading place between East Neck and Santapaug. Quoriac is treated as an abbreviated form rather than a separately translated name.

Why Place Names Matter

“Geographical names are more than labels on maps and road signs; they convey aspects of the history and promise of an area that might otherwise be overlooked or forgotten by visitors and later generations.”

— BC Geographical Names Office, British Columbia’s Geographical Naming Principles, Policy and Procedures (2017), Background, PDF page 2
land_loss_content: Guscomquorom connects a Babylon neck with movement across land and water. The name preserves an Indigenous geography of crossings, trails, and wading places beneath later English labels such as East Neck and Great East Neck.
whereintheworld_content: The map placement uses the modern Great East Neck / West Babylon area as a public reference, not an exact historic deed boundary or crossing point.
